picks.title: 09/06/26 Blind Spots: Gossip
picks.summary: Homily from the Twenty-third Sunday in Ordinary Time. Gossip is speaking of someone else's faults and flaws with no intention to help them at all. Gossip can be easy to recognize when someone else is doing it—and surprisingly difficult to see in ourselves. There are times when we need to speak about another person’s faults. But when there is no intention to help them, our words reveal a blind spot of our own. Mass Readings from September 6, 2026: Ezekiel 33:7-9 Psalm 95:1-2, 6-7, 8-9Romans 13:8-10 Matthew 18:15-20]]>
picks.reason: Homily addressing the moral issue of gossip from a Catholic perspective.

picks.showTitle: Sunday Homilies with Fr. Mike Schmitz
picks.title: 08/30/26 Forfeit
picks.summary: Homily from the Twenty-second Sunday in Ordinary Time. You cannot become the person you were meant to be without the Cross. No one likes to lose. But there is a difference between getting beaten and forfeiting. Because Jesus has won, the only way we can lose our souls is if we forfeit. Mass Readings from August 30, 2026: Jeremiah 20:7-9 Psalm 63:2-9Romans 12:1-2 Matthew 16:21-27]]>
picks.reason: Homily on spiritual growth through embracing the Cross and avoiding forfeiting salvation.

picks.showTitle: The Catechism in a Year (with Fr. Mike Schmitz)
picks.title: Day 247: The Weight of Sin (2026)
picks.summary:
We can consider the variety of sins in light of their gravity or seriousness. In doing so, we see that some sins weaken charity while others destroy it. The first we call venial sins, the second mortal. Our very freedom makes possible this rejection of God. Yet, God’s mercy has no limits. God can and will forgive every sin of which we repent. Fr. Mike invites all listeners to seek this forgiveness and go to Confession. Today’s readings are Catechism paragraphs 1854-1864.

picks.reason: Explains sin's gravity and God's mercy within Catholic moral theology.

picks.showTitle: The Catechism in a Year (with Fr. Mike Schmitz)
picks.title: Day 242: The Virtue of Faith (2026)
picks.summary:
The origin, motive, and object of the theological virtues are God himself.  Today, we dive into the theological virtues, beginning with the virtue of Faith. Fr. Mike unpacks the meaning and purpose of the virtue of Faith and emphasizes that Faith is deeply rooted in trust in God. Lastly, Fr. Mike reminds us that Faith should be lived out along with Hope, and Love, and also professed to those who do know yet know God. Today’s readings are Catechism paragraphs 1812-1816.

picks.reason: Teaches the theological virtue of Faith rooted in trust in God, per Catholic doctrine.
